markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **recent-prefix training with moderate confusable negatives**, preserving one BERT4Rec per category. This is an untested hypothesis; the supplied diagnostics establish failure patterns, not validation gains.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Broad resemblance often displaces specific matches. Training should distinguish plausible alternatives without assuming compatibility labels exist. (2) Older interests can obscure current priorities. Recent-prefix targets offer observable supervision for immediate choices, although timestamps cannot reveal mood. (3) Industrial and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. Their negative lower-tail margins motivate better discrimination; embedding scores near 0.5 do not justify collapse remedies.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec already includes terminal masking [1]. Increasing its exposure is an alignment experiment, not a novel objective. (2) Recency sampling favors recent targets while retaining older examples [2]. Its transfer to BERT4Rec remains unverified. (3) EMM motivates mixing hard and random negatives [3]. Similarity filtering can limit mining intensity but cannot establish that an unobserved item is truly negative.

The conceptual framework links **temporal alignment → prefix sampling**, **specificity → confusable-negative selection**, and **ranking reliability → measured margins plus fixed validation HR@10**. Missing compatibility labels remain a gap across all three directions.

Three feasible ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Increase terminal-mask exposure [1,2] | 2/6/6/6/2 | Grounded; targets immediate choice | Weak direct specificity supervision |
| B. Introduce moderate title-confusable negatives [3] | 4/7/7/8/4 | Targets broad-match confusion | False negatives; limited temporal alignment |
| C. Apply B to recent terminal-prefix examples [1–3] | 4/8/8/8/5 | Couples current context with fine discrimination | Interacting changes complicate attribution |

These assessments cover each dimension: originality reflects modest recombination; potential and alignment reflect the stated mechanisms; difficulty reflects sampler complexity. None represents measured improvement.

**Select C.** It explicitly targets two user failures: broad matches outranking specific choices, and historical interests outweighing current priorities. It also targets negative lower-tail margins, especially in the two weaker datasets. It cannot infer equipment ownership, mood, or compatibility absent supporting observations.

Keep ordinary Cloze batches and gradually introduce terminal-prefix batches. Choose training-only prefix endpoints using a uniform/recency mixture; replace the endpoint target with the reserved mask and discard subsequent interactions. Mix uniform negatives with moderately title-similar candidates, excluding the target, known training positives, and duplicates. Use bounded pairwise-loss weight for mined negatives; this is a ranking objective, not an estimate of full softmax.

Ablate A, B, then C only within budget. Select exclusively by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, 200 epochs maximum, 200 batches/epoch, diagnostic interfaces, and checkpoint/predictor consistency. Appended-mask inference reads the final nonpadding position, never nonpadding-count minus one.

idea.description: Train each category's single BERT4Rec with a curriculum that adds recent terminal-prefix examples and moderate title-confusable negatives to ordinary masked-item training.
idea.motivation: Address broad plausible recommendations displacing specific choices and insufficient attention to recent priorities. Quantitatively, target weak lower-tail positive–negative separation in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics without misinterpreting near-zero mean embedding cosine similarity as collapse.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied baseline and its ordinary Cloze objective. For added terminal examples, sample a training-history endpoint, remove all later interactions, and replace the target with the reserved mask. Start with terminal-example fraction 0.25 and ramp to 0.50 over the first quarter of training; these are initial hypotheses. Construct title-overlap candidate pools using only permitted public text, without pretrained weights. Sample from a moderate similarity band, mix at most 25% mined negatives with uniform negatives, and exclude known training positives and duplicates. For terminal examples, use mean softplus(negative_score-positive_score), with mined-negative contribution capped at 25% of the aggregate loss weight. Do not apply uniform LogQ correction to mined samples or claim full-softmax equivalence. Unobserved items can still be false negatives. Use one model and one selected checkpoint per category; text overlap affects training sampling only. Retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, the supplied splits, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Keep log2feats, item_emb, predict_score, ModelView, DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt compatible. Probe only valid masked-target positions and report missing category metadata as unavailable. Preserve the predictor writer and appended-mask construction; for left padding compute the maximum occupied position, never count(nonpadding)-1. No baseline source was supplied here, so this is implementation pseudocode rather than a claimed drop-in train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    initialize supplied BERT4Rec with seed 42
    build title-overlap sampling index from permitted metadata
    for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
        terminal_fraction = ramp(0.25, 0.50)
        for batch in range(200):
            if sample_terminal_example(terminal_fraction):
                history = sample_training_user_history()
                endpoint = sample_endpoint(uniform_recency_mixture)
                target = history[endpoint]
                sequence = left_pad(history[:endpoint] + [MASK], L)
                negatives = unique_mixture(uniform_items, moderate_title_neighbors(target))
                exclude target and known training positives from negatives
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                position = max_index_where(sequence != PAD)
                loss = bounded_weight_pairwise_loss(features[position], target, negatives)
            else:
                sequence, masked_targets = baseline_cloze_batch()
                loss = baseline_masked_target_loss(sequence, masked_targets)
            optimizer_step(loss)
        evaluate using unchanged validation protocol
        retain one selected checkpoint for this category
    export matching architecture and weights through predictor writer
select experimental configuration using macro validation HR@10 only

originality.positive: Connects recency-conditioned terminal supervision with moderate confusable-negative sampling in a constraint-compatible BERT4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Terminal masking, recency sampling, and mixed negative mining already exist; the contribution is their specific combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides a testable path toward learning immediate, fine-grained choices using available interaction histories and public text.
future_potential.negative: Sparse titles and false negatives may limit gains; neither recency nor lexical similarity establishes actual user intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the backbone and inference architecture; changes concentrate in sampling and training loss.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires efficient similarity pools, exclusion handling, controlled loss weighting, and separate ablations within the shared GPU budget.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides bidirectional masked-item learning and appended-mask next-item prediction.
Includes last-item masking to align training with next-item inference.
limitations: Increasing terminal-task exposure is an adaptation of an existing mechanism.
Does not establish improvements for the proposed curriculum on this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Recency-based Sampling of Sequences
contributions: Motivates favoring recent prediction targets while preserving some older-target supervision.
limitations: The supplied summary concerns other backbones; transfer to BERT4Rec requires validation.
Recency is an imperfect proxy for present needs.

limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish gains for BERT4Rec or the four target categories.
